ffc.description: The program your connected apps run to reach your sites. This app finds it on your PATH or where the ffc installers put it, and can install the latest release for you; it never ships its own copy.
ffc.noAnswerManager: Running it failed ({{error}}). Reinstalling it with {{manager}} usually fixes this.
ffc.noAnswer: Running it failed ({{error}}). Installing it again usually fixes this.
ffc.updateBody: Updating replaces the ffc above, where it is. Restart your connected apps afterwards so they use the new version.
ffc.autoCheck: The app looks for a newer ffc once a day; Check for updates looks right away. You can also run {{command}} in a terminal.
ffc.installHere: Install it here, or run this in a terminal yourself:
ffc.notCompared: This ffc is not a release build, so it cannot be compared with the releases.
ffc.updateWithManager: It was installed with {{manager}}, so update it there: run this in a terminal.
ffc.updateWithCommand: The app does not replace this copy of ffc. Update it by running this in a terminal:
ffc.noRelease: No ffc release was found on GitHub. Try again later.

update.easiestWay: The easiest way to install it: run this in {{terminal}}. It checks the download, closes this app, installs the new version over it and opens it again, with no security warning to click through.
update.orDownload: Or download it from GitHub and install it over this one.
update.downloadFromGitHub: Download it from GitHub and install it over this one.
update.upToDateTitle: The app is up to date

about.summary: Connects your Frappe and ERPNext sites to the AI apps on your computer, using the ffc command line underneath. Made by Foxmayn. For Windows and macOS.
about.independent: Foxmayn makes this app independently. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Frappe Technologies.

history.title: History
history.intro: Conversations are kept on this computer. Exports never contain your API keys.
history.help: Older conversations are deleted when the app starts and once a day, archived ones too. Pinned conversations and ones being answered are always kept.
history.confirmBody: Conversations with no message for {{days}} days are deleted from this computer when the app next starts or within a day, and then every day. This cannot be undone. Pin a conversation to keep it.

explore.p1: Which apps and versions are installed on this site?
explore.p2: Show the 10 most recent Sales Invoices with their customer, total and status.
explore.p3: What fields does the Customer DocType have, and which are required?

profile.title: Profiles
profile.intro: A profile sets what the assistant is for: its tools, its mode and its instructions. It can only narrow what a site allows, never widen it.
profile.editorBody: The site's own rules still apply: anything the site does not allow stays refused.
profile.deleteBody: Conversations that use this profile switch to Explore (read only).
profile.modeHelp: The stricter of this and the conversation's switch applies.
profile.toolsetsHelp: None checked means the default tool sets (core and lifecycle).
profile.callMethodHelp: Lets the assistant call server methods, only when the conversation asks before changes and the site allows it.
profile.keepHistoryHelp: Off: conversations with this profile are not kept and are removed when the app next starts.

installFfc.readyRestart: Version {{version}} is ready. Restart your connected apps to use it.
installFfc.manager: ffc was installed with {{manager}}, so {{manager}} updates and reinstalls it, not this app.
installFfc.managerRun: ffc was installed with {{manager}}, so {{manager}} updates and reinstalls it, not this app. Run this in a terminal, then restart your connected apps so they use the new version.
installFfc.updateBody: This downloads the latest ffc release from GitHub, checks its signature and replaces the ffc {{version}} at {{path}}. A development build of ffc is left alone and a new copy is installed for your user instead.
installFfc.installBody: Connected apps use ffc, a small program from Foxmayn, to talk to your Frappe sites. This downloads the latest ffc release from GitHub, checks its signature and installs it for your user only.
installFfc.whereWindows: It installs ffc to your user's Programs folder and adds that folder to your PATH.
installFfc.whereSignature: The download is refused unless its signature matches Foxmayn's release key. You can also install it yourself in a terminal:
installFfc.restartApps: Restart your connected apps (quit them fully) so they use the new version.
installFfc.alsoTerminal: You can also install it yourself in a terminal:

wsl.title: ffc settings found in WSL
wsl.bodyOne: Your Linux environment ({{distro}}) has its own ffc settings. This app manages the Windows settings only, and the two are not synced. Add the sites here too if you want Windows apps to use them.
wsl.bodyMany: One of your Linux environments has its own ffc settings. This app manages the Windows settings only, and the two are not synced. Add the sites here too if you want Windows apps to use them.
